issues.description: Naming is inconsistent across PR title, CHANGELOG, and check directory (single vs multiple network interfaces).
issues.detail: The PR title and CHANGELOG entry describe 'multiple network interfaces' detection, but the directory, class, file, and CheckID use 'single_network_interface'. A reader cannot tell from the name whether PASS means 'has one' or 'has many', and grep will fail six months from now. Pick one convention and apply it consistently across docs, metadata, and code.

issues.description: GKE detection by name prefix 'gke-' is a brittle string-match where a real signal exists.
issues.detail: Using instance.name.startswith('gke-') is a special-case heuristic any user can spoof, and legitimate GKE nodes with custom prefixes will FAIL. The general signal is available: the GKE-managed label ('goog-gke-node') or managed-instance-group reference. Capture that on the Instance model and key the exemption off it.

issues.description: Zero-interface branch silently PASSes with no test coverage.
issues.detail: When interface_count == 0, the check falls through to PASS with a 'has no network interfaces' message. A VM with zero NICs is degenerate/anomalous, not compliant with a 'single interface' rule. No test exercises this branch. Either remove it, FAIL/MANUAL it explicitly, or document why PASS is correct and add a test.

issues.description: Mutable default '[]' on Pydantic field network_interfaces should use Field(default_factory=list).
issues.detail: network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = [] reads as a Python mutable-default footgun. Pydantic v1 copies defaults per-instance, but the idiom is fragile across versions and inconsistent with codebase style. Prefer Field(default_factory=list) and match surrounding conventions.

issues.description: interface_names is computed unconditionally even when unused by PASS and zero-NIC branches.
issues.detail: interface_names = [nic.name for nic in instance.network_interfaces] runs for every instance, but only the multi-NIC FAIL path consumes it. Build the list inside the branch that uses it; minor readability and zero-work cleanup.

issues.description: ip_forward exemption promised in metadata Notes is not implemented; public_ip duplicates NIC data.
issues.detail: Metadata Notes mention network virtual appliances as legitimate multi-NIC, and ip_forward already exists on Instance — either honor it (MANUAL when ip_forward=True and multi-NIC) or drop the claim. Also fold accessConfigs/natIP into the new NetworkInterface struct and derive public_ip from it, so there is one pass and one source of truth.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the check is small, tested, and structurally sound, but ships with three blocking issues a maintainer would bounce: inconsistent naming between 'single' and 'multiple' across PR/CHANGELOG/code, a brittle GKE detection that string-matches on 'gke-' name prefix when API labels are available, and a silent PASS for the zero-interface degenerate case with no test. Secondary cleanups: use Field(default_factory=list) for the new Pydantic field, hoist interface_names computation into the branch that uses it, and either honor the ip_forward exemption the metadata advertises or remove the claim. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — fix the GKE signal, reconcile naming/state docs, and handle the zero-NIC branch explicitly.
